posts.note: Year-end run-down of rapid-acting treatments (AI scribes, SAINT, dTMS, psychedelics, Radial and competitors). Five calls: insurance coverage as the next step, coverage in 2026, psychedelics 'almost' here, market room for more companies, dTMS scalability. Company descriptions ('hard at work bringing ... to patients') and the RAMHT ticket call were not logged.

Review of a JAMA Network Open Brazilian cohort on mortality after a household suicide. One own-newsletter plan ('I'm sure I will again'). 'We should follow the survivors of suicide just as closely' is normative with no predictive reading; not logged.
Short tribute sharing Nolan Williams' ibogaine TED talk. One statement: his work will save lives for years to come.

Advice column for health professionals on not prescribing for lovers and family. One newsletter-series plan and one generic 'for a certainty' prediction that ex-partners will weaponize a license. Conditional advice ('if a vengeful lover decides to report you ... will be averted', 'likely to make you less enthusiastic') folded here, not logged.

Grief essay on Nolan Williams and the magnesium-ibogaine PTSD paper. One borderline generic clinical claim (severe trauma will not resolve on its own). 'It must be covered, accessible, and available in a private setting' is normative; 'is predictive of treatment outcome' is a present-tense finding; neither logged.

Reprise of the Flow Neuroscience EMPOWER at-home tDCS trial breakdown, republished on the day of FDA approval. Six statements: Neurolief device to market soon, drug-first paradigm death-knell, devices are the future, sham must improve in future trials, tDCS not expected to match SAINT, and a flagged normative call for trials if approved. 'All we need is some possible way to actually pay for depression treatment that isn't a pill' is a wish; not logged.

Radial $50M Series A announcement with the full press release. Eight statements, all own-org except the General Catalyst investor quote. Epidemiology rates ('80% of people will have a neuropsychiatric illness', '13% of teenage girls ... will attempt suicide', '1 in 5 people will eventually get cancer') are rate statements, not forecasts; not logged. 'Not anymore' and 'Their goal is to make transformative care accessible to all' are rhetoric and goals.
Past-tense clinical memoir about a patient with Cotard's delusion; no forward-looking statements.

Recycled memoir of childhood suicidality and bipolar diagnosis plus a RAMHT 2026 event promo. One personal 'never' statement and two RAMHT event statements. 'Go back to bringing breakthrough treatments to the world at Radial on Monday' is a personal schedule item, not logged; Dr. Zeitlin's 1999 prediction is past and third-party.

statements.quote: The next step, of course, is broad insurance coverage.
statements.context: After noting that accelerated dTMS and adolescent dTMS (BrainsWay) are now FDA-cleared, the author says the next step for these treatments is broad insurance coverage, and asks readers to call their health plan, HR department and government.
statements.note: Expectation framed as a sequence ('next step'); restates a long-running coverage call.

statements.quote: The Psychedelics Are Here…Almost.
statements.context: Section heading in the run-down of rapid-acting treatments. Under it the author cites MindMed MM-120 phase II data, COMP360 psilocybin progress, and AtaiBeckley 5-MeO-DMT data. Implies psychedelic treatments will arrive soon.
statements.note: Section heading; borderline. Implicit call that psychedelic approval or availability is near.

statements.quote: It’s more true than ever, but insurance coverage still lags—I’m looking at you, 2026.
statements.context: Closing of the run-down: people deserve to get well sooner; insurance coverage for rapid-acting treatments still lags, and the author points to 2026 as the year coverage should catch up.
statements.note: Exhortation with a predictive reading: the author expects or hopes coverage moves in 2026. Borderline wish vs forecast.

statements.quote: There is, in my opinion, more than enough suffering for the number of companies above and more.
statements.context: After listing Radial and competitors (Beckley Clinical, Stella Centers, Salma Health, Everbright Health, Hope Theraputics, First Tracks, Big Leap, Osmind) working to scale rapid-acting treatments, the author says the market has room for all of them and more.
statements.note: Market-size call implying these companies can all be sustained; the author is Radial CMO.

statements.quote: This makes the treatment scalable and thus accessible to more people who need it.
statements.context: FDA clearance of an accelerated dTMS protocol and adolescent dTMS (BrainsWay, no fMRI targeting needed) makes the treatment scalable and, the author says, accessible to more people who need it.
statements.note: Present tense with a forward implication that access will broaden; borderline.

statements.quote: I’ve written about cohort studies before, and I’m sure I will again.
statements.context: Aside while introducing the JAMA Network Open household-suicide cohort study (100 Million Brazilian Cohort); the author plans to write about cohort studies again in the newsletter.
statements.note: Own-newsletter content plan.

statements.quote: He was loved, and his love and rigor will be saving lives for years to come.
statements.context: Tribute to Nolan Williams after his death, sharing his ibogaine TED talk; the author says Williams' work (SAINT, ibogaine research) will keep saving lives for years.
statements.note: Eulogy claim about the lasting impact of Williams' science.

statements.quote: this is the first of “Owen's Letters to the Health Professionals,” not a name that I spent a lot of time on.
statements.context: The author launches a new newsletter series addressed to health professionals, prompted by Derek of 5HT; this post is the first, and more are implied ('this article and other articles like it').
statements.note: Own-newsletter series plan.

statements.quote: I do know, for a certainty, that some of our relationships will end, and tension will arise. I know humans will seek to exact revenge. That revenge will be calibrated to hurt us. Everything you have ever done will be reinterpreted with malice. Reliably, your professional license will be used against you.
statements.context: Advice to prescribers: some relationships will end and ex-partners will use the clinician's license against them; the setup for the rule never to provide medical care for people who are not patients in your practice.
statements.note: Generic, truism-like prediction about human behavior framed as certain; borderline forecast, logged for recall.

statements.quote: it's not gonna work itself out on its own reliably
statements.context: On severe trauma, after the magnesium-ibogaine PTSD paper from Nolan Williams' group: the author says you have to get treatment that will heal the trauma; untreated severe trauma will not resolve reliably on its own.
statements.note: Generic clinical claim about the course of untreated trauma; borderline forecast.

statements.quote: We are (in full disclosure) bringing a depression treatment device to market soon.
statements.context: Disclosure that the author is CMO of Radial and of Neurolief, an at-home neuromodulation company, which is bringing a depression treatment device to market soon.
statements.note: Own-org call; implies regulatory clearance and launch of a Neurolief depression device.

statements.quote: consider this the death-knell for daily drug-first or daily drug-only biological treatment for depression as a paradigm
statements.context: On Flow Neuroscience obtaining FDA approval for its at-home tDCS device for depression; the author calls it the end of the daily drug-first or drug-only paradigm for biological depression treatment.
statements.note: Paradigm-shift call: drug-first depression treatment will decline.

statements.quote: Our editorial point of view, at TFPs, is that medical devices that modulate the brain is the future.
statements.context: Reprise of the original article on the Flow tDCS trial; the newsletter's editorial stance that brain-modulating medical devices are the future of psychiatric treatment, contrasted with Elon Musk's self-driving promises.
statements.note: Restatement of a long-running editorial thesis.

statements.quote: It also calls for subsequent trials to answer these questions for practicing clinicians if the device is approved.
statements.context: After listing the EMPOWER trial's narrow exclusion criteria (no prior TMS, ECT, ketamine, hospitalization, bipolar, PTSD, OCD), the author says further trials are needed to answer real-world questions if the Flow device is approved. Written before approval; republished on approval day.
statements.note: Normative call with a conditional on approval; logged with flags. Related: 'I am advocating for the phase 3 trial and subsequent studies ... to have broader inclusion and exclusion criteria.'

statements.quote: The sham? It will need to be improved to preserve the blind in future trials!
statements.context: Functional unblinding in the EMPOWER at-home tDCS trial (77.6% in active vs 59.3% in sham guessed active; skin redness far higher in active); the author says the sham must improve in future trials.
statements.note: Requirement statement about future trials; borderline normative, weak predictive reading.

statements.quote: And we shouldn’t expect that from tDCS, based on prior studies.
statements.context: Answering the question whether the Flow device is at-home SAINT TMS: no. The author says tDCS should not be expected to reach SAINT-level results (effect size here 0.37), based on prior tDCS studies.
statements.note: Negative expectation about tDCS efficacy relative to SAINT TMS.

statements.quote: We see a future where psychiatric treatments work
statements.context: Radial launch post; the author (Radial CMO) describes the company's vision of a future where psychiatric treatments work 'shockingly well' and depression treatment ends depression.
statements.note: Own-org vision statement; borderline forecast.

statements.quote: We will be working together both before and after whatever job we have at this very moment—medicine is a long road.
statements.context: On the other companies in the rapid-acting treatment space (Beckley Clinical, Salma, Stella Centers, Acacia Clinics, Hope Therapeutics, Osmind, Big Leap, Everbright), many run by friends; the author expects continued collaboration across companies and jobs.
statements.note: Generic industry-collaboration prediction.

statements.quote: This fundraising will support the company’s plans to expand nationally in 2026, growing both its clinic network and technology partnerships.
statements.context: Radial press release (December 9, 2025) republished by the author as 'our press release': $50 million Series A led by General Catalyst; Radial operates seven clinics in six states and plans national expansion in 2026.
statements.note: Press release text; own-org expansion plan with a dated horizon.

statements.quote: The company is building a national network of clinics that accept most major forms of insurance, including Medicare,Tricare, VA-CCN, Aetna, Cigna, United, and many Blues plans.
statements.context: Radial press release: the company is building a national in-network clinic network across major payers, with clinical infrastructure, reimbursement tools and decision support around brain medicine.
statements.note: Present progressive with a forward implication; press release text.

statements.quote: For patients this means the most effective combination of therapies are available to everyone who needs them, for clinicians this means focusing on providing that care, and for payors this means better outcomes and less ultimate cost for even the most complex patients.
statements.context: Radial press release: the claimed effects of Radial's infrastructure, reimbursement tools and decision support for patients, clinicians and payers, including lower total cost for payers.
statements.note: Marketing claim in the press release; implies payers will see lower total cost; borderline forecast.

statements.quote: Radial is here to change that. When we have tools for the right clinical workflows and insurance pathways, people can access therapies that help them get better far sooner.
statements.context: John Capecelatro, Radial CEO and co-founder, quoted in the press release the author republishes; claims Radial will fix the healthcare system's lag behind rapid-acting treatments and that the right tools will let people access these therapies sooner. Cites remission rates of 50-60% and up to 78%.
statements.note: Quoted third party (CEO) inside the author's own company's release, shared as 'our press release'; treated as adopted.

statements.quote: We believe this work can meaningfully expand access to effective mental health care.
statements.context: Reva Nohria, Partner at General Catalyst (Series A lead investor), quoted in the Radial press release on Radial's potential to expand access to brain-based treatments.
statements.note: Quoted investor; the author republishes the release without explicitly adopting this line.

statements.quote: We’re taking what we know from years of clinical research and turning it into care that any patient can access.
statements.context: Owen Muir, Radial CMO, quoted in the press release: Radial was built to close the research-to-practice gap and will turn clinical research into care any patient can access.
statements.note: Own-org mission claim with a forward implication; borderline.

statements.quote: I will never know what happened at the end of my sister’s life.
statements.context: Memoir: the author's sister Alison Muir died of an opiate overdose after a prior suicide attempt; whether the overdose was intentional is unclear, and the author says he will never know.
statements.note: Personal, non-market 'never' statement.

statements.quote: Rapid-Acting Mental Health Treatment (RAMHT) Returns January 11th in San Francisco.
statements.context: Footer promo: the author's RAMHT live newsletter event returns January 11 (2026) in San Francisco; a ticket link and the RAMHT 2026 sponsor and speaker list follow.
statements.note: Own event; dated.

statements.quote: And a few more to be announced soon! It will be off the hook, as usual.
statements.context: After the RAMHT 2026 sponsor and speaker list; more sponsors and speakers are to be announced soon, and the event will be a success as in prior years.
statements.note: Own event; promotional.
